s1.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with rash and hypotension in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: erythematous patches and thin plaques with telangiectases and hyperpigmentation
intravascular atypical cells on skin biopsy
key_facts: patient has a history of chronic pulmonary coccidiomycosis
patient was being treated with fluconazole
pembrolizumab treatment was stopped 3 months prior due to a morbilliform reaction
new skin eruption appeared different from previous reaction
patient has fever and hypotension
white blood cell count is 4100/μL
absolute neutrophil count is 2940/μL
hemoglobin level is 8.2 g/dL
platelet count is 62 ×10^3/μL
blood culture results showed no growth at 1 week
serum β-D-glucan, galactomannan, Coccidioides antibody, and immunodiffusion results were negative

shortlist.label: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Skin biopsy findings of intravascular atypical cells and patient's symptoms of fever, hypotension, and rash

shortlist.label: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of fever, hypotension, and rash, along with laboratory findings of low white blood cell count, low platelet count, and low hemoglobin level

shortlist.label: Cytokine release syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of pembrolizumab treatment and symptoms of fever, hypotension, and rash

shortlist.label: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's laboratory findings of low platelet count and low white blood cell count

shortlist.label: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's laboratory findings of low platelet count and low white blood cell count

shortlist.label: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of fever, hypotension, and rash, along with laboratory findings of low white blood cell count and low platelet count

shortlist.label: Anaplastic large cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of fever, hypotension, and rash, along with skin biopsy findings of atypical cells

shortlist.label: Natural killer/T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of fever, hypotension, and rash, along with skin biopsy findings of atypical cells

raw.rationale: The patient's skin biopsy findings showing intravascular atypical cells, along with the presence of fever, hypotension, and a new skin eruption, are consistent with intravascular large B-cell lymphoma. The negative infectious disease workup and the lack of growth in blood cultures also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
rejected.why: While the patient has fever, hypotension, and cytopenias, the skin biopsy findings and the lack of other specific diagnostic criteria make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Cytokine release syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and timeline do not align with the typical presentation of cytokine release syndrome, which is often associated with recent immunotherapy or infection.

rejected.label: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
rejected.why: The patient's laboratory results do not show evidence of widespread coagulation abnormalities, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
rejected.why: The patient's clinical presentation and laboratory results do not align with the typical features of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, such as schistocytes on blood smear and elevated lactate dehydrogenase.

rejected.label: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The patient's skin biopsy findings and clinical presentation do not align with the typical features of angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma, such as generalized lymphadenopathy and autoimmune phenomena.

rejected.label: Anaplastic large cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The patient's skin biopsy findings do not show the characteristic large anaplastic cells of anaplastic large cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: Natural killer/T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The patient's clinical presentation and skin biopsy findings do not align with the typical features of natural killer/T-cell lymphoma, such as nasal or facial involvement and specific immunophenotypic markers.
